extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology (readers of a topology textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and criteria for computing fundamental groups of spaces (knot complements, cell complexes, surfaces) using deformation retraction, van Kampen’s theorem, attaching cells, and covering space theory. Includes presentations (generators/relations), lifting properties, and classification of covering spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity condition for torus-knot parametrization
rubrics_metrics.description: One needs to assume that m and n are relatively prime in order for the map f to be injective. Without this assumption f would be d–to–1 where d is the greatest common divisor of m and n, and the image of f would be the knot K_{m/d,n/d}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If m and/or n are negative this only changes K to a mirror-image knot. The relatively-prime condition is also tied to embeddability of the associated 2-complex X_{m,n} into R^3 (X_{m,n} embeds in R^3 only when m and n are relatively prime); e.g. X_{2,2} is the Klein bottle and nonembeddable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactification to S^3 preserves π1 for knot complements
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacing R^3 by its one-point compactification S^3 does not affect π1: the inclusion R^3 − K → S^3 − K induces an isomorphism on π1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses van Kampen: write S^3 − K as union of R^3 − K and an open ball B containing the compactification point; both B and B ∩ (R^3 − K) are simply-connected (the latter homeomorphic to S^2 × R), so inclusion induces isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deformation retract of knot complement onto a 2-complex Xm,n
rubrics_metrics.description: S^3 − K deformation retracts onto a 2-dimensional complex X = X_{m,n} homeomorphic to the quotient of a cylinder S^1 × I under identifications (z,0)∼(e^{2π i/m}z,0) and (z,1)∼(e^{2π i/n}z,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct X as union of two mapping cylinders Xm and Xn (quotients of S^1×[0,1/2] and S^1×[1/2,1]). Geometric embedding uses decomposing S^3 into two solid tori and flowing within meridian disks to produce deformation retractions onto these mapping cylinders; adjust flows to agree on overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute π1(X) via van Kampen and mapping cylinders
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply van Kampen to X = Xm ∪ Xn where Xm and Xn deformation retract onto circles and Xm ∩ Xn is a circle. A loop in the intersection represents m times a generator in Xm and n times a generator in Xn, so π1(X) has presentation with generators a,b and relation a^m = b^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus define G_{m,n} = ⟨a,b | a^m = b^n⟩. If m or n = 1 the group is infinite cyclic. The argument uses identification of how the intersection loop maps into each mapping cylinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and center of G_{m,n}
rubrics_metrics.description: The element a^m = b^n commutes with a and b, so the cyclic subgroup C generated by this element lies in the center; after quotienting by C the group is Z_m * Z_n, whose center is trivial, hence C is the entire center of G_{m,n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From this one deduces C is infinite cyclic (elements a and b have infinite order when m,n>1, shown elsewhere). Use Exercise facts about free products to conclude trivial center of Z_m * Z_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining m and n from the group G_{m,n}
rubrics_metrics.description: The integers m and n are uniquely determined by the group Z_m * Z_n, hence also by G_{m,n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue via abelianization: abelianization of Z_m * Z_n is Z_m × Z_n of order m n, so the product m n is determined. Exercise result: torsion elements of Z_m * Z_n are conjugate into one of the factors Z_m or Z_n, so the maximum order of torsion elements equals max(m,n); both m and n are recovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonembeddability criterion for Xm,n in R^3
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2-complex X_{m,n} can be embedded in R^3 only when m and n are relatively prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes classical non-embeddability (e.g., Klein bottle cannot embed in R^3). Reference given to remarks following later corollary and to Example 1.44 for related facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wirtinger presentation algorithm for knot complements (outline)
rubrics_metrics.description: An algorithm for computing a presentation for π1(R^3 − K) for an arbitrary smooth or PL knot K (the Wirtinger presentation): position the knot nearly flat, build a deformation-retract 2-complex X from the table top rectangle, strips R_i over arcs on the table, and squares S_ℓ over crossings; there is one generator x_i per strip R_i and for each square S_ℓ a relation of the form x_i x_j x_i^{-1} = x_k corresponding to the crossing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: identify strips and crossing squares as in figures; orientation of K gives correct signs. Use this presentation to show abelianization of π1(R^3 − K) is Z. This is given as an explicit, constructive method (exercise 22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on π1 of attaching 2-cells (Proposition 1.26(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is obtained from X by attaching 2-cells via maps ϕ_α: S^1 → X, then the inclusion X ↪ Y induces a surjection π1(X,x0) → π1(Y,x0) whose kernel is the normal subgroup N generated by the loops γ_α ϕ_α γ_α (where γ_α are chosen paths from basepoint to the attachment basepoints). Thus π1(Y) ≅ π1(X)/N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N is independent of the choice of connecting paths (changes give conjugate elements). Proof proceeds by enlarging Y to a convenient space Z and applying van Kampen to cover {A,B} with B contractible and A deformation-retracting to X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-dimensional cell attachments do not change π1 (Proposition 1.26(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is obtained from X by attaching n-cells with n>2, then the inclusion X ↪ Y induces an isomorphism π1(X,x0) ≅ π1(Y,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: in the van Kampen argument the relevant intersection pieces deformation-retract onto S^{n-1} so have trivial π1 when n>2.

rubrics_metrics.name: π1 depends only on the 2-skeleton (Proposition 1.26(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a path-connected cell complex X the inclusion of the 2-skeleton X^2 ↪ X induces an isomorphism π1(X^2,x0) ≅ π1(X,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X is finite-dimensional use induction via part (b); for infinite-dimensional use compactness of the image of loops to reduce to finite stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of surface groups via cell structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The orientable surface M_g of genus g has a cell structure giving π1(M_g) ≅ ⟨a_1,b_1,…,a_g,b_g | [a_1,b_1]…[a_g,b_g]⟩ (i.e., free group on 2g generators modulo the normal subgroup generated by the product of commutators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1-skeleton is wedge of 2g circles (free group), 2-cell attached along product of commutators. Use abelianization to deduce invariants (e.g., rank 2g). Similar presentations for nonorientable surfaces (words a_1^2 … a_g^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting genus via abelianization (Corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M_g ≃ M_h then their fundamental groups are isomorphic, so their abelianizations are isomorphic; the abelianization of π1(M_g) is Z^{2g}, hence genus g is determined by π1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus surfaces of different genus are not homotopy equivalent (nor homeomorphic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Realizing any group as π1 of a 2-dimensional cell complex (Corollary 1.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every group G there is a 2-dimensional cell complex X_G with π1(X_G) ≅ G, constructed from a presentation of G by attaching 2-cells to a wedge of circles according to relators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose generators g_α and relators r_β; construct wedge of circles for generators and attach 2-cells along loops specified by relators. Examples show how specific groups (e.g., Z_n) yield familiar spaces (RP^2 when n=2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shrinking wedge example: π1 can be uncountable and more complicated
rubrics_metrics.description: The union X of circles C_n of radius 1/n centered at (1/n,0) (the shrinking wedge) has fundamental group mapping onto the direct product ∏ Z (uncountable), showing π1(X) is uncountable and far larger than the countable free group of an infinite wedge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct retractions r_n: X→C_n inducing surjections ρ_n: π1(X)→Z and take product ρ: π1(X)→∏ Z which is surjective. Also π1(X) is nonabelian and even maps onto free groups on finite sets (use retractions collapsing small circles). Reference: Cannon & Conner 2000 and Shelah 1988 theorem on compact metric spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and local condition for covering spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering space p: X → X is a map such that each x ∈ X has an open neighborhood U with p^{-1}(U) a union of disjoint open sets (sheets), each mapped homeomorphically onto U by p. The number of sheets over U is the cardinality of p^{-1}(x) and is locally constant (hence constant if X is connected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology: U is evenly covered; sheets over U are the connected components of p^{-1}(U). p need not be surjective in the general definition (allow empty preimages over disconnected U). Examples include the helicoid projection to R^2 − {0} and p(z)=z^n map S^1→S^1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing covering graphs for wedge of circles via 2-orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering spaces of X = S^1 ∨ S^1 may be described as graphs with a 2-orientation: at each vertex there are four edge ends labeled a and b with specified incoming/outgoing orientations, and a covering map p sends labeled edges homeomorphically to corresponding edges of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For finite connected graphs with an even number (four) of edge ends at each vertex, produce a 2-orientation by finding an Eulerian circuit and alternating labels along the circuit; the union of a-edges and b-edges becomes collections of circles whose orientations give the required structure. Infinite-graph generalizations cited (König).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification theorem for connected covering spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a one-to-one correspondence between connected covering spaces of X (up to isomorphism) and conjugacy classes of subgroups of π1(X,x0). If basepoints are kept track of, pointed connected coverings correspond to actual subgroups (not just conjugacy classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For graphs an isomorphism of covers is a graph isomorphism preserving labels and orientations. Changing basepoint in the cover corresponds to conjugating the subgroup. Symmetry (deck transformation) group of a cover is isomorphic to quotient π1(X)/H when H is normal; maximal symmetry ↔ normal subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy lifting property for covering spaces (Proposition 1.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a covering space p:X→X and a homotopy f_t: Y→X with a lift f_0 available, there exists a unique homotopy of lifts f_t: Y→X lifting f_t and starting at the chosen lift of f_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property (covering homotopy property) implies path-lifting and uniqueness of lifts; used frequently to lift homotopies, paths, and maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path lifting and uniqueness of lifts (corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each path f:I→X and each chosen starting point in the fiber p^{-1}(f(0)), there is a unique lift of f starting at that point. Uniqueness implies lifts of constant paths are constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking Y=I in the homotopy lifting proposition gives path-lifting; endpoints of lifted homotopies remain fixed if endpoints project to constant paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of p_* and characterization of its image (Proposition 1.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering p:(X,x0)→(X,x0) the induced map p_*:π1(X,x0)→π1(X,x0) is injective. Its image consists exactly of homotopy classes of loops in X based at x0 whose lifts to X starting at x0 are loops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses homotopy lifting: an element in kernel would lift to a nullhomotopy contradicting uniqueness. Conversely, any loop whose lift is a loop belongs to the image; homotopy lifting shows homotopic loops preserve liftability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of sheets equals index of subgroup (Proposition 1.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a path-connected covering space p:(X,x0)→(X,x0), the number of sheets equals the index [π1(X,x0): p_*(π1(X,x0))].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct bijection from cosets H[g] of H=p_*(π1(X)) to points in the fiber p^{-1}(x0) by lifting representative loops; path-connectedness ensures surjectivity and uniqueness shows injectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting criterion for maps (Proposition 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given covering p:(X,x0)→(X,x0) and a map f:(Y,y0)→(X,x0) with Y path-connected and locally path-connected, a lift f:(Y,y0)→(X,x0) exists iff f_*(π1(Y,y0)) ⊂ p_*(π1(X,x0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'only if' direction is immediate. For existence pick for each y a path γ from y0 to y and lift f∘γ starting at x0; independence of choice of γ follows from hypothesis about subgroup inclusion and uniqueness of lifts (use homotopy lifting to verify well-definedness). Local path-connectedness is required for technical reasons in lifting argument.
